subject: petroleum fly
title: A Fly Lives Inside Pools of Crude Oil, and It Eats What Drowns There

scenes.text: Nearly nothing survives crude oil. This fly lives in it.
The petroleum fly, described in 1899 from the La Brea tar pits in Los Angeles. Its larvae live submerged in the oil.
They eat insects trapped in the sticky surface. Their guts are full of petroleum, and it doesn't harm them.
In summer the oil hits 38 degrees Celsius. In the lab, larvae even survived 50 percent turpentine.
The adults dance across the tar. Nobody has ever seen them mate.
So crude oil kills almost everything. Almost.

description:
The petroleum fly, Helaeomyia petrolei, spends its larval life submerged in pools of natural crude oil.
It was described in 1899 from the La Brea tar pits in Los Angeles. The larvae are found only in the oil, feeding on insects and other arthropods trapped in its sticky surface; their guts are visibly full of petroleum, yet they are unharmed. The oil's surface reaches 37 to 38 degrees Celsius in summer, and in laboratory tests the larvae tolerated 50 percent turpentine or xylene. Adults walk across the asphalt, and their mating has never been observed.
What's the harshest place you've seen an animal live?
thumbnail_text: THE FLY THAT LIVES IN OIL
first_comment: The larvae can't live on oil alone; they need the drowned insects. Would you call that the world's worst diet or the world's best hiding place?
